verdict.root_cause: An automated image-reference change on cart at 04:11:10 [tr_2b13800c9e60] took the service down: cart logged routine traffic until 04:11:06, then a clean graceful shutdown at 04:11:09 with no restart or startup banner for the rest of the window [tr_b0f7fb64e3a5]. With cart absent, its endpoints were withdrawn, which matches frontend's symptoms exactly — checkout failing with INTERNAL wrapping a name resolver that returned zero addresses for cart, plus gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE host-unreachable, progressing from dropped connections to no connection possible [tr_dfc8f3bbf81c]. Frontend's error ratio broke from an exactly-flat-zero baseline at 04:12:46, ninety seconds after cart stopped [tr_e7416da6ce5f]. Cart emits zero error-coded spans but has intervals with no span traffic at all [tr_058f9905ad2e] — the signature of a service that is gone rather than broken. The running artifact on cart is one that does not stay up, so this is a bad deploy on cart; frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout are downstream victims.
verdict.reasoning: The image apply at 04:11:10 and cart's shutdown at 04:11:09 are the same minute [tr_2b13800c9e60, tr_b0f7fb64e3a5], and frontend's change point follows at 04:12:46 [tr_e7416da6ce5f] — a clean causal ordering. Frontend's errors are all client-side gRPC statuses toward a downstream, with no panic, restart or resource error of its own, and its change log is empty across onset [tr_dfc8f3bbf81c, tr_be27a2e7b078], so frontend is the noticer, not the culprit. The specific statuses — zero-address resolution and host-unreachable rather than DEADLINE_EXCEEDED — rule out a slow dependency and point at a withdrawn one [tr_dfc8f3bbf81c]. Cart's flat-zero error ratio with undefined (no-traffic) samples [tr_058f9905ad2e] fits absence, not failure. The clean trace sample [tr_2ab49179448e] is survivorship-biased: it samples the ~98% of requests that succeeded in a bursty 2.2%-mean window, so it refutes latency but not intermittent unavailability.
open_questions: Cart's logs end at shutdown with the window closing ~5.5 minutes later, so whether the hotfix image failed to start, crashed unseen, or was never scheduled is unsettled — as is whether the artifact is broken or the deploy churn merely left cart down.
Nothing confirms that 172.18.0.24:7070 is cart; if it is another backend, only the zero-address resolution error ties cleanly to cart.
No availability, replica-count or restart-count metrics were returned for cart [tr_058f9905ad2e]; 11 of 13 services in the blast radius were never examined.

alternatives.root_cause: The repeated apply/revert flap itself is the fault — an automation control loop fighting over cart's image reference, leaving it intermittently unscheduled.
alternatives.why_not: Same class and fix; demoted only because it asserts an automation-loop mechanism the evidence does not show. The flap is recorded [tr_2b13800c9e60] but reverts already failed four times to end the cycle, so pinning cart to a known-good image is the operative action either way.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart is running but cut off from the network, so callers see unreachable endpoints while cart itself continues.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned service keeps logging and complains it cannot reach things; cart instead logged an orderly multi-stage shutdown and then went silent [tr_b0f7fb64e3a5], and its cart-store lines show no connection errors at all.

proposal.expected_effect: Cart redeployed at its prior image tag and recreated. Within ~2 minutes cart's Loki stream should show a startup banner and routine ValkeyCartStore lines again (it has emitted nothing since the graceful shutdown at 04:11:09). Frontend's checkout INTERNAL 'resolver returned zero addresses for cart' and gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE lines should cease, and frontend's error ratio should decay back toward its exactly-zero baseline within one or two 5m rate windows.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if cart logs no startup banner within ~120s (prior tag also unbootable, or cart is never scheduled); or cart comes up but frontend keeps logging host-unreachable to 172.18.0.24:7070, which was never confirmed to be cart; or platform-automation reapplies the hotfix and cart shuts down again, meaning the apply/revert flap must be stopped before any rollback holds.
proposal.risk: Four prior reverts of this same tag did not end the flap, so this may be overwritten within minutes and merely adds churn. If the hotfix image is actually fine and the deploy controller simply left cart stopped, rolling back changes the running artifact for no reason and obscures the real fault. Cart's in-memory state is discarded on recreate.
proposal.blast_radius: cart only, plus its callers during the recreate: checkout (direct), and frontend / frontend-proxy on the checkout and cart paths see resets for a few seconds. Load-generator traffic on those paths will register the blip.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service failure spanning frontend, proxy, and checkout with load-generator impact indicates real user-facing breakage, not noise. No open incidents to duplicate; cause could lie in any of several checkout/frontend dependencies, so no fault class is implied yet.
